sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Carteret County?
sections.html:
Record it at the Register of Deeds office in the County Administrative Building, 302 Courthouse Square, Beaufort, NC 28516. Records can be inspected there between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday.

The office describes itself as the legal custodian of land records and land transactions in the county. It probates, records, indexes and images them into the permanent record, and everything it holds is public except military discharges. The county also runs an online database where land records can be viewed and printed, which is the quickest way to pull your vesting deed before a sale.

One detail applies to older paperwork. The county's real estate page says Books 301 through 514 are on aperture cards, and a cancelled deed of trust is stamped on the card itself. If you need proof that an old loan was released and the online image does not show it, call the office rather than assuming the lien is still open.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees in Carteret County?
sections.html:
The county prints its fee list on one page, and the real estate lines match the uniform schedule in G.S. 161-10. The office accepts cash, credit or debit card, money orders and cashier's checks for recording.

Document or serviceFee as the county prints it
General instruments, excluding deeds of trust and mortgages$26 for the first 15 pages, $4 for each additional page
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64 for the first 35 pages, $4 for each additional page
Plats$21 per sheet
Satisfaction instrumentsNo fee per statute
Document containing multiple instrumentsAdditional $10
Nonstandard documentsAdditional $25
Certified copies$5 for the first page, $2 for each additional page
Uncertified copies$0.25
Excise tax valuation$2 per $1000.00 of sales price

The same page lists an extra $10 for each added index reference on an assignment, and no fee to record a military discharge. The fee page is headed with an effective date of October 1, 2019, so ask the office if anything has changed since.

sections.h2: How do I keep a Carteret County deed from being charged as nonstandard?
sections.html:
Follow the county's published recording standards, because a document that misses them is still recorded but costs an extra $25. The office's penalty paragraph says it will record the nonconforming document after collecting the $25 nonstandard fee along with the normal recording fee.

  • Paper: 8 1/2 x 11 or 8 1/2 x 14.
  • Top of page one: a blank margin of 3 inches.
  • Remaining sides of page one and all sides of later pages: a 1/4 inch blank margin, per the standards page.
  • Print: black on white, in a legible font, with 10 points as the smallest size treated as legible.
  • Pages: one-sided only.
  • Heading: the type of instrument at the top of the first page.

The fee page contradicts the standards page on side margins. It says the minimum side margin went back to one-half inch under Session Law 2019-117, effective October 1, 2019, while the standards page still shows 1/4 inch. Ask the office which one it applies before you print the deed. Blanks and corrections may be filled in by pen, and the office has discretion to treat slightly small type as legible and waive the fee.

sections.h2: Who pays the transfer tax when a Carteret County house sells?
sections.html:
The seller pays. State law puts the excise tax on the transferor and requires payment to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded, as G.S. 105-228.30 spells out.

The rate in the statute is $1.00 for each $500.00, or fraction of $500.00, of the consideration or value. Carteret County's fee page expresses the same thing as $2 per $1000.00 of the sales price. The settlement agent normally takes the amount from the seller's proceeds, so it shows as a line on the seller's side of the closing statement.

Recording itself matters as much as the tax. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance does not bind lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies. A buyer who does not record leaves the door open to later claims.

sections.h2: How do Carteret County property taxes interact with a sale?
sections.html:
Carteret County bills property tax once a year, due September 1 and delinquent after January 5, and any balance on the parcel has to be paid or credited at closing. The county mailed more than 82,000 bills in August 2026, and the county rate for fiscal year 2026-27 is 22.5 cents per $100 of assessed value.

Owners in Beaufort, Bogue, Cape Carteret, Cedar Point, Emerald Isle, Morehead City and Peletier get a single bill that carries both county and town tax. After January 5, the county adds 2% for January and 0.75% for each later month. Unpaid real estate taxes are advertised between March 1 and June 30, and the county says that advertisement is the first step toward foreclosure.

The county reappraised real property with an effective date of January 1, 2025. A taxpayer who disputes a value has 30 days from the notice date to appeal, then goes to the Board of Equalization and Review, which has nine Carteret County residents including two alternates. A fuller walk through of those steps is on our Carteret County property tax guide.

sections.h2: What other papers does the Carteret County office handle for an inherited house?
sections.html:
The office is also the custodian of birth, death and marriage records for events in the county, and it can issue certified copies. Its fee page lists a certified death certificate copy at $10 and a certified marriage license copy at $10, and it says not everyone can obtain a certified copy, so ask about the eligibility rules first.

For an heir selling a parent's house, the usual packet is the death certificate, the vesting deed and a certified copy of any recorded instrument that affects the land. Certified copies of recorded documents are $5 for the first page and $2 for each additional page. If an estate is involved, ask the Carteret County Clerk of Superior Court what the estate file requires.

The office is a recording office, says it cannot advise in any legal capacity, and cannot supply legal forms or answer questions about what an instrument does in law. Use an attorney for drafting.

sections.h2: What does Carteret County look like for a seller?
sections.html:
Carteret County is a coastal county of about 507.60 square miles of land, and the Census Bureau estimates 70,469 residents on July 1, 2025, up 4.1% from the 2020 base. The Census counts 54,293 housing units against 31,977 households for 2020-2024, so the county has well over 20,000 more homes than households.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home, 2020-2024: $333,300.
  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate: 74.7%.
  • Median gross rent: $1,108.
  • Median household income: $72,322.
  • Residents 65 and over: 30.1%.

Those figures are from the Census QuickFacts page. If you own here but live elsewhere, documents can be mailed to the Beaufort address above, and the county's online database lets you check the record from a distance.

faqs.q: Does the Carteret County Register of Deeds charge to record a satisfaction of a deed of trust?
faqs.a: No. The county's fee page lists satisfaction instruments at no fee per statute, so paying off a loan does not cost anything to record the release.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a standard deed in Carteret County?
faqs.a: It costs $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each additional page, based on the county's printed fee list. A deed that breaks the recording standards adds $25, and a document holding several instruments adds $10.

faqs.q: What forms of payment does the Carteret County register of deeds accept?
faqs.a: The office takes cash, credit or debit cards, money orders and cashier's checks for recording. Mail goes to 302 Courthouse Square, Beaufort, NC 28516.

faqs.q: Can I view Carteret County deeds online?
faqs.a: Yes. The county says land records can be viewed and printed from its Register of Deeds Online Database. Books 301 through 514 are on aperture cards, so call the office about cancellation details for those older records.

faqs.q: What is the Carteret County transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: The county prints it as $2 per $1000.00 of the sales price, which equals the state rate of $1.00 per $500.00. The seller pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.
